v.rationale: I found no real requirement bugs in any of the three. All test suites pass (19/18/12). Each one passed my probes for a savepoint rollback inside a committed outer transaction, a stale second model instance trying to ship again, a non-JSON POST getting 409, array input getting 422, and the mail rendering the tracking number. Rank 1 is impl-1. It pairs an atomic conditional UPDATE with afterCommit mail, maps the domain exception to 409 centrally in bootstrap, wires a route ->can() policy, and has the most thorough Pest tests, including the case where the shipment insert fails. Rank 2 is impl-2. Its core logic matches impl-1, but its exception is an HTTP ConflictHttpException inside a domain model, it adds global bootstrap config the task didn't need, and one rollback test calls DB::rollBack() by hand. Rank 3 is impl-3. Its concurrency handling is correct and it is the only one robust to a null is_staff. It still loses on idioms: authorization sits in FormRequest::authorize instead of a policy, the controller builds the 409 with try/catch, the in-memory model is left dirty, ExampleTests were deleted, and its tests share beforeEach state and cover fewer edge cases. The policies in impl-1 and impl-2 return a nullable is_staff typed as bool. The non-staff probe got a 500 because the user was built in memory without the column. A real Sanctum request reloads the user from the DB, so I counted this as a robustness note, not a bug.
